cards.front: What are the four chambers of the heart?
cards.back: Right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium and left ventricle

cards.front: Which side of the heart pumps blood to the lungs?
cards.back: The right side

cards.front: Which valve lies between the left atrium and left ventricle?
cards.back: The mitral (bicuspid) valve

cards.front: Which valve lies between the right atrium and right ventricle?
cards.back: The tricuspid valve

cards.front: What does the aortic valve prevent?
cards.back: Backflow of blood from the aorta into the left ventricle

cards.front: What are the heart sounds S1 and S2?
cards.back: S1 is closure of the AV valves, S2 is closure of the semilunar valves

cards.front: Where does the sinoatrial node sit?
cards.back: In the wall of the right atrium, the heart's pacemaker

cards.front: What is the normal resting heart rate?
cards.back: 60 to 100 beats per minute
The volume of blood ejected by the ventricle in one beat
Heart rate times stroke volume
The stretch of the ventricle at the end of diastole
The resistance the ventricle must overcome to eject blood

cards.front: What does the P wave on an ECG represent?
cards.back: Atrial depolarisation

cards.front: What does the QRS complex represent?
cards.back: Ventricular depolarisation

cards.front: What does the T wave represent?
cards.back: Ventricular repolarisation
Acute myocardial infarction
An irregularly irregular rhythm with no clear P waves

cards.front: What is the most common cause of a heart attack?
cards.back: Rupture of an atherosclerotic plaque with a clot in a coronary artery

cards.front: Which artery supplies the anterior wall of the left ventricle?
cards.back: The left anterior descending artery
Chest pain from reduced blood flow to the myocardium
The heart cannot pump enough blood for the body's needs

cards.front: What are the signs of left-sided failure?
cards.back: Breathlessness, pulmonary oedema and crackles

cards.front: What are the signs of right-sided failure?
cards.back: Raised jugular venous pressure, ankle oedema and hepatomegaly
An extra sound caused by turbulent blood flow

cards.front: What murmur is typical of aortic stenosis?
cards.back: An ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids
Infection of the heart valves
Inflammation of the pericardium, with pain that improves on sitting forward
Fluid in the pericardial sac compressing the heart
Hypotension, raised JVP and muffled heart sounds
Blood pressure persistently above 140/90 mmHg
Diastolic pressure plus a third of the pulse pressure
A fast feedback loop that keeps blood pressure steady

cards.front: What does the renin-angiotensin system do?
cards.back: Raises blood pressure by vasoconstriction and sodium retention

cards.front: What is a congenital septal defect?
cards.back: A hole in the wall between the heart's chambers
VSD, pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta and right ventricular hypertrophy

cards.front: What is a patent ductus arteriosus?
cards.back: A fetal vessel that fails to close after birth
The more the heart is filled, the harder it contracts
The percentage of blood in the ventricle that is pumped out each beat
The sequence of contraction and relaxation, called systole and diastole

cards.front: Which coronary artery supplies the SA node most often?
cards.back: The right coronary artery

cards.front: What is a pacemaker used for?
cards.back: To treat a slow or irregular heartbeat
An ultrasound scan of the heart
Damage to heart muscle, raised after a heart attack
A mesh tube that holds a coronary artery open
